name: Chepala Pulusu
subtitle: a fiery tamarind fish stew, sour and hot with no coconut in sight

ingredients.note: seer, king fish or any firm-fleshed fish that holds its shape

ingredients.qty: a lime-sized ball, soaked in 400ml hot water

ingredients.note: the signature bitter note of a pulusu
balances the tamarind, not for sweetness
thickens the gravy the traditional way

prepNotes: Rub the fish steaks with 1/2 tsp turmeric and a little salt and leave 15 minutes, then rinse. This takes off the sharp smell.
Soak the tamarind in hot water for 20 minutes, squeeze out the pulp and strain.
Use a wide, shallow pan so the fish sits in one layer — it is never stirred, only swirled.

steps.text: Heat the groundnut oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then the cumin, fenugreek and curry leaves.
steps.tip: Fenugreek turns bitter within seconds of browning. Count to five and move on.

steps.text: Add the chopped onion and fry 8 minutes over medium heat until soft and lightly browned at the edges.
Stir in the crushed garlic, ginger and slit green chillies and fry 2 minutes until the raw smell lifts.
Lower the heat, add the chilli powder, coriander powder and remaining turmeric with 2 tbsp water, and fry 2 minutes until the oil shows red at the edges.
Pour in the strained tamarind water with the salt and jaggery and bring to a boil.
Boil uncovered 10 minutes to cook out the tamarind and reduce the gravy by about a quarter.
steps.tip: Cook the tamarind down before the fish goes in. Fish added early falls apart in a raw-tasting gravy.

steps.text: Slide the fish steaks in in a single layer and spoon gravy over them. Do not stir.
Simmer uncovered 8 to 10 minutes, swirling the pan by the handle every few minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes at the edge.
steps.tip: Move the pan, not the fish. A spoon breaks the steaks every time.

steps.text: If you want it thicker, trickle in the slaked rice flour and simmer 2 minutes more.
Take off the heat, scatter the coriander and rest 15 minutes before serving with plain rice.
steps.tip: Pulusu genuinely needs the rest — the sourness settles and the fish takes up the gravy.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated and the flavour deepens overnight. Reheat gently over low heat without stirring, tilting the pan to baste the fish. Do not freeze.
